title: Night Frequency
brief: A dialogue management game: you are a night-shift radio operator replying to callers under a countdown. Every reply costs time, trust moves up or down, and some replies unlock only after you hear a caller out. GameState keeps time_left, trust, replies and ended. Finish the shift with trust at least three to win; ending lower is a loss.
artDirection: Warm radio-desk lamplight over a dark studio, callers as readable silhouettes, a legible countdown and trust meter, reply buttons with clear pressed states.

obligations.description: Choosing a reply sends it and raises replies.
Sending a reply lowers time_left from its starting 120.
The countdown reaching zero ends the shift and sets ended.
The shift is won only when trust is at least three at the final tick, and lost below it.
obligations.unsupported: A win criterion must start false and become true on one property; trust can already start above the bar, and an end-of-shift comparison over trust plus the clock is a conjunction the current vocabulary cannot bind.

obligations.description: Choosing a reply advances the conversation to that reply's next node with its own text.
obligations.unsupported: Dialogue nodes and text are strings, and the change they cause is a named transition; the vocabulary reads numeric thresholds and generic changes only.

obligations.description: A reply that has not unlocked cannot be chosen and costs no time.
obligations.unsupported: Invalid-action handling needs a negative route and an unchanged time_left; the vocabulary can only prove a value changed, not that a rejected choice left it alone.
